title: Retinal Oxygen Function After Radiation Therapy
brief_summary: The investigators propose using retinal oximetry to assess for abnormalities in regional retinal oxygen consumption in previously- irradiated patients, and relate these abnormalities to changes in regional retinal function (i.e. visual field abnormalities). Since different regions of retina receive different radiation doses, the investigators will assess for a dose response as well.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. ≥ 18 years of age at the time of radiation therapy (no upper age limit)
2. History of radiation therapy delivered at UNC-CH or Rex Hospital to the vicinity of the retina(s) ≥ 2 months prior to enrollment
3. Estimated average dose to at least one quadrant of one retina ≥ 30 Gy

Exclusion Criteria:

1. History of diabetes, retinal vascular occlusions, glaucoma, retinitis pigmentosa, occipital stroke or any other ophthalmologic or systemic problem that may confound visual field results.
2. Residual tumor within the visual pathway: retina, optic nerves, optic chiasm, optic radiations and brain.
study_population: Adult patients with a history of radiation therapy for a tumor in the vicinity of the retina(s) at the Department of Radiation Oncology, UNC-CH.
condition: A History of Radiation Therapy for a Tumor in the Vicinity of the Retina(s)
